top.en: If you don't understand the draft, just go watch Chu Jun's video on Bilibili. He completely predicted every direction and detail of the draft. The coaches and players must have analyzed DK's gameplay and realized their laning phase is average, and they like to play for the late game and teamfight comebacks. So BLG decided not to care about lane strength in the draft, whether they were ahead or behind, trusting that player skill could make up for it. The focus was entirely on the team composition's scaling curve—mid-to-late game comps. But who knew that once in-game, even with a winning draft, the opponent couldn't win? They didn't even get a dragon in two games with winning lanes, and instead, BLG took a bunch of dragons. It feels just like IG vs TES, exactly the same. These two teams must have been scrimming each other; the draft direction and game content are identical. Both are weak-lane comps, but once in-game, they rely on player ability and individual star power to turn losing matchups into winning ones. It's insane. Still, no popping champagne yet, stay vigilant.

Playing like this isn't just being bad; either you're following orders, someone is match-fixing, or you really need to see a doctor.
